meta.title: Vite
meta.description: From an empty Vite + React app to a working schedule, in three steps.

goal: Render the schedule in a Vite application, styled, with items of your own. Vite needs no configuration for this: the package ships ESM and a plain CSS file, both of which Vite handles as they are.

points: A Vite + React project, JavaScript or TypeScript. npm create vite@latest gives you one.
React 18.2 or 19, and the matching react-dom. They are peer dependencies, so they stay yours.
Node 22 or newer to build with.

install.title: Install the package
install.text: One dependency, no others. Everything it needs is either a peer or already in the box.

stylesheet.title: Import the stylesheet once
stylesheet.text: The stylesheet is a normal CSS file, imported wherever you import your global CSS — usually the entry module. It is the only import that has to happen exactly once.

render.title: Render a schedule
render.text: An item needs an id, a start and a title; a level is what gives it its color and its place in the order. Everything else has a default.

result.text: Run npm run dev. You get one shift around the current time, two items in it, and a now indicator where the clock is. From here, Shifts and dates changes the shape of the day and Theming changes how it looks.

points: The schedule is unstyled: the stylesheet import is missing, or it is in a module that is never loaded. It has to be imported, not linked.
A build that treats CSS imports in dependencies as an error: keep the import in your own entry module rather than importing it from a shared package of yours.
Two Reacts in the bundle — usually a linked local package — produce the hook error React itself reports. npm ls react finds it.
